# Resource: stripe_credit_note

A reduction of a finalized invoice's amount, which can credit the customer's balance or refund a payment. Stripe refuses a credit note on a draft invoice. Set `status` to `void` to void an issued credit note, which gives the invoice back the amount it credited; an invoice cannot be voided while an issued credit note remains. Only `memo` and `metadata` change after creation.

~> A credit note can move real money. In a live-mode Stripe account, creating or changing one, including setting its `status`, fails at plan time unless the provider sets `allow_live_money_movement = true`. Reading or importing one never does. The provider asks Stripe for the account's mode. See the Managing Test Data guide.

~> Stripe cannot delete a credit note; set `status` to `void` to void one. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the credit note, fail at plan time. To stop managing a credit note, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_customer" "acme" {
  email = "billing@acme.example"
}

resource "stripe_invoiceitem" "setup_fee" {
  customer = stripe_customer.acme.id
  amount   = 5000
  currency = "usd"
}

resource "stripe_invoice" "setup" {
  customer                       = stripe_customer.acme.id
  currency                       = "usd"
  collection_method              = "send_invoice"
  days_until_due                 = 30
  pending_invoice_items_behavior = "include"
  status                         = "open"

  depends_on = [stripe_invoiceitem.setup_fee]
}

# Takes 10.00 off the open invoice.
resource "stripe_credit_note" "goodwill" {
  invoice = stripe_invoice.setup.id
  reason  = "order_change"
  memo    = "Goodwill credit"

  lines = [{
    type        = "custom_line_item"
    description = "Goodwill credit"
    quantity    = 1
    unit_amount = 1000
  }]
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `invoice` - (Required) ID of the invoice. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.

The following arguments are optional:

* `amount` - (Optional) The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the total amount of the credit note. One of `amount`, `lines`, or `shipping_cost` must be provided. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `credit_amount` - (Optional) The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the amount to credit the customer's balance, which will be automatically applied to their next invoice. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `effective_at` - (Optional) The date when this credit note is in effect. Same as `created` unless overwritten. When defined, this value replaces the system-generated 'Date of issue' printed on the credit note PDF. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `email_type` - (Optional) Type of email to send to the customer, one of `credit_note` or `none` and the default is `credit_note`. Possible values: `credit_note`, `none`. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `lines` - (Optional) Line items that make up the credit note. One of `amount`, `lines`, or `shipping_cost` must be provided. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. See [`lines`](#lines) below.
* `memo` - (Optional) The credit note's memo appears on the credit note PDF.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `out_of_band_amount` - (Optional) The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the amount that is credited outside of Stripe. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `reason` - (Optional) Reason for issuing this credit note, one of `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, `order_change`, or `product_unsatisfactory` Possible values: `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, `order_change`, `product_unsatisfactory`. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `refund_amount` - (Optional) The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the amount to refund. If set, a refund will be created for the charge associated with the invoice. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `refunds` - (Optional) Refunds to link to this credit note. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. See [`refunds`](#refunds) below.
* `shipping_cost` - (Optional) When shipping_cost contains the shipping_rate from the invoice, the shipping_cost is included in the credit note. One of `amount`, `lines`, or `shipping_cost` must be provided. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. See [`shipping_cost`](#shipping_cost) below.
* `status` - (Optional) Status of this credit note, one of `issued` or `void`. Learn more about [voiding credit notes](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/invoices/credit-notes#voiding). Possible values: `void`.

<a id="lines"></a>
### `lines`

The `lines` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - (Optional) The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the gross amount being credited for this line item, excluding (exclusive) tax and discounts.
* `description` - (Optional) Description of the item being credited.
* `discount_amount` - (Read-Only) The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the discount being credited for this line item.
* `discount_amounts` - (Read-Only) The amount of discount calculated per discount for this line item See [`lines.discount_amounts`](#lines.discount_amounts) below.
* `id` - (Read-Only) Unique identifier for the object.
* `invoice_line_item` - (Optional) ID of the invoice line item being credited
* `livemode` - (Read-Only) If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - (Read-Only) String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `credit_note_line_item`.
* `pretax_credit_amounts` - (Read-Only) The pretax credit amounts (ex: discount, credit grants, etc) for this line item. See [`lines.pretax_credit_amounts`](#lines.pretax_credit_amounts) below.
* `quantity` - (Optional) The number of units of product being credited.
* `tax_amounts` - (Optional) See [`lines.tax_amounts`](#lines.tax_amounts) below.
* `tax_rates` - (Optional) The tax rates which apply to the line item.
* `taxes` - (Read-Only) The tax information of the line item. See [`lines.taxes`](#lines.taxes) below.
* `type` - (Required) The type of the credit note line item, one of `invoice_line_item` or `custom_line_item`. When the type is `invoice_line_item` there is an additional `invoice_line_item` property on the resource the value of which is the id of the credited line item on the invoice. Possible values: `custom_line_item`, `invoice_line_item`.
* `unit_amount` - (Optional) The cost of each unit of product being credited.
* `unit_amount_decimal` - (Optional) Same as `unit_amount`, but contains a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places.

<a id="lines.discount_amounts"></a>
### `lines.discount_amounts`

The `lines.discount_amounts` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - The amount, in cents (or local equivalent), of the discount.
* `discount` - The discount that was applied to get this discount amount.

<a id="lines.pretax_credit_amounts"></a>
### `lines.pretax_credit_amounts`

The `lines.pretax_credit_amounts` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - The amount, in cents (or local equivalent), of the pretax credit amount.
* `credit_balance_transaction` - The credit balance transaction that was applied to get this pretax credit amount.
* `discount` - The discount that was applied to get this pretax credit amount.
* `type` - Type of the pretax credit amount referenced. Possible values: `credit_balance_transaction`, `discount`.

<a id="lines.tax_amounts"></a>
### `lines.tax_amounts`

The `lines.tax_amounts` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - (Required)
* `tax_rate` - (Required)
* `taxable_amount` - (Required)

<a id="lines.taxes"></a>
### `lines.taxes`

The `lines.taxes` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - The amount of the tax, in cents (or local equivalent).
* `tax_behavior` - Whether this tax is inclusive or exclusive. Possible values: `exclusive`, `inclusive`.
* `tax_rate_details` - Additional details about the tax rate. Only present when `type` is `tax_rate_details`. See [`lines.taxes.tax_rate_details`](#lines.taxes.tax_rate_details) below.
* `taxability_reason` - The reasoning behind this tax, for example, if the product is tax exempt. The possible values for this field may be extended as new tax rules are supported. Possible values: `customer_exempt`, `not_available`, `not_collecting`, `not_subject_to_tax`, `not_supported`, `portion_product_exempt`, `portion_reduced_rated`, `portion_standard_rated`, `product_exempt`, `product_exempt_holiday`, `proportionally_rated`, `reduced_rated`, `reverse_charge`, `standard_rated`, `taxable_basis_reduced`, `zero_rated`.
* `taxable_amount` - The amount on which tax is calculated, in cents (or local equivalent).
* `type` - The type of tax information. Possible values: `tax_rate_details`.

<a id="lines.taxes.tax_rate_details"></a>
### `lines.taxes.tax_rate_details`

The `lines.taxes.tax_rate_details` attribute supports:

* `tax_rate` - ID of the tax rate

<a id="refunds"></a>
### `refunds`

The `refunds` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount_refunded` - (Optional) Amount of the refund that applies to this credit note, in cents (or local equivalent).
* `payment_record_refund` - (Optional) The PaymentRecord refund details associated with this credit note refund. See [`refunds.payment_record_refund`](#refunds.payment_record_refund) below.
* `refund` - (Optional) ID of the refund.
* `type` - (Optional) Type of the refund, one of `refund` or `payment_record_refund`. Possible values: `payment_record_refund`, `refund`.

<a id="refunds.payment_record_refund"></a>
### `refunds.payment_record_refund`

The `refunds.payment_record_refund` attribute supports:

* `payment_record` - (Required) ID of the payment record.
* `refund_group` - (Required) ID of the refund group.

<a id="shipping_cost"></a>
### `shipping_cost`

The `shipping_cost` attribute supports:

* `amount_subtotal` - (Read-Only) Total shipping cost before any taxes are applied.
* `amount_tax` - (Read-Only) Total tax amount applied due to shipping costs. If no tax was applied, defaults to 0.
* `amount_total` - (Read-Only) Total shipping cost after taxes are applied.
* `shipping_rate` - (Optional) The ID of the ShippingRate for this invoice.
* `taxes` - (Read-Only) The taxes applied to the shipping rate. See [`shipping_cost.taxes`](#shipping_cost.taxes) below.

<a id="shipping_cost.taxes"></a>
### `shipping_cost.taxes`

The `shipping_cost.taxes` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - Amount of tax applied for this rate.
* `rate` - Tax rates can be applied to [invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing/taxes/tax-rates), [subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) and [Checkout Sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/use-manual-tax-rates) to collect tax. Related guide: [Tax rates](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) See [`shipping_cost.taxes.rate`](#shipping_cost.taxes.rate) below.
* `taxability_reason` - The reasoning behind this tax, for example, if the product is tax exempt. The possible values for this field may be extended as new tax rules are supported. Possible values: `customer_exempt`, `not_collecting`, `not_subject_to_tax`, `not_supported`, `portion_product_exempt`, `portion_reduced_rated`, `portion_standard_rated`, `product_exempt`, `product_exempt_holiday`, `proportionally_rated`, `reduced_rated`, `reverse_charge`, `standard_rated`, `taxable_basis_reduced`, `zero_rated`.
* `taxable_amount` - The amount on which tax is calculated, in cents (or local equivalent).

<a id="shipping_cost.taxes.rate"></a>
### `shipping_cost.taxes.rate`

The `shipping_cost.taxes.rate` attribute supports:

* `active` - Defaults to `true`. When set to `false`, this tax rate cannot be used with new applications or Checkout Sessions, but will still work for subscriptions and invoices that already have it set.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the tax rate for your internal use only. It will not be visible to your customers.
* `display_name` - The display name of the tax rates as it will appear to your customer on their receipt email, PDF, and the hosted invoice page.
* `effective_percentage` - Actual/effective tax rate percentage out of 100. For tax calculations with automatic_tax[enabled]=true, this percentage reflects the rate actually used to calculate tax based on the product's taxability and whether the user is registered to collect taxes in the corresponding jurisdiction.
* `flat_amount` - The amount of the tax rate when the `rate_type` is `flat_amount`. Tax rates with `rate_type` `percentage` can vary based on the transaction, resulting in this field being `null`. This field exposes the amount and currency of the flat tax rate. See [`shipping_cost.taxes.rate.flat_amount`](#shipping_cost.taxes.rate.flat_amount) below.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `inclusive` - This specifies if the tax rate is inclusive or exclusive.
* `jurisdiction` - The jurisdiction for the tax rate. You can use this label field for tax reporting purposes. It also appears on your customer’s invoice.
* `jurisdiction_level` - The level of the jurisdiction that imposes this tax rate. Will be `null` for manually defined tax rates. Possible values: `city`, `country`, `county`, `district`, `multiple`, `state`.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `tax_rate`.
* `percentage` - Tax rate percentage out of 100. For tax calculations with automatic_tax[enabled]=true, this percentage includes the statutory tax rate of non-taxable jurisdictions.
* `rate_type` - Indicates the type of tax rate applied to the taxable amount. This value can be `null` when no tax applies to the location. This field is only present for TaxRates created by Stripe Tax. Possible values: `flat_amount`, `percentage`.
* `state` - [ISO 3166-2 subdivision code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2), without country prefix. For example, "NY" for New York, United States.
* `tax_type` - The high-level tax type, such as `vat` or `sales_tax`. Possible values: `amusement_tax`, `communications_tax`, `digital_excise_tax`, `gst`, `hst`, `igst`, `jct`, `lease_tax`, `mass_transit_parking_tax`, `parking_tax`, `pst`, `qst`, `retail_delivery_fee`, `rst`, `sales_tax`, `service_tax`, `utility_users_tax`, `vat`.

<a id="shipping_cost.taxes.rate.flat_amount"></a>
### `shipping_cost.taxes.rate.flat_amount`

The `shipping_cost.taxes.rate.flat_amount` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount of the tax when the `rate_type` is `flat_amount`. This positive integer represents how much to charge in the smallest currency unit (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).
* `currency` - Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `amount_shipping` - This is the sum of all the shipping amounts.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `customer` - ID of the customer.
* `customer_account` - ID of the account representing the customer.
* `customer_balance_transaction` - Customer balance transaction related to this credit note.
* `discount_amount` - The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the total amount of discount that was credited.
* `discount_amounts` - The aggregate amounts calculated per discount for all line items. See [`discount_amounts`](#discount_amounts) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `number` - A unique number that identifies this particular credit note and appears on the PDF of the credit note and its associated invoice.
* `pdf` - The link to download the PDF of the credit note.
* `post_payment_amount` - The amount of the credit note that was refunded to the customer, credited to the customer's balance, credited outside of Stripe, or any combination thereof.
* `pre_payment_amount` - The amount of the credit note by which the invoice's `amount_remaining` and `amount_due` were reduced.
* `pretax_credit_amounts` - The pretax credit amounts (ex: discount, credit grants, etc) for all line items. See [`pretax_credit_amounts`](#pretax_credit_amounts) below.
* `subtotal` - The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the amount of the credit note, excluding exclusive tax and invoice level discounts.
* `subtotal_excluding_tax` - The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the amount of the credit note, excluding all tax and invoice level discounts.
* `total` - The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the total amount of the credit note, including tax and all discount.
* `total_excluding_tax` - The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the total amount of the credit note, excluding tax, but including discounts.
* `total_taxes` - The aggregate tax information for all line items. See [`total_taxes`](#total_taxes) below.
* `type` - Type of this credit note, one of `pre_payment` or `post_payment`. A `pre_payment` credit note means it was issued when the invoice was open. A `post_payment` credit note means it was issued when the invoice was paid. Possible values: `mixed`, `post_payment`, `pre_payment`.
* `voided_at` - The time that the credit note was voided.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing a credit note whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_credit_note.goodwill

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_credit_note.goodwill
```

The credit note stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a credit note using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_credit_note.goodwill
  id = "cn_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_credit_note.goodwill
  identity = {
    id = "cn_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the credit note.

Using `terraform import`, import a credit note using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_credit_note.goodwill cn_123
```
